indicator: Full fibre broadband coverage (% of premises)
notes: Original indicator label ('Broadband coverage data') renamed to match what's actually reported. Ofcom's local-authority-level breakdown is genuinely published (via its interactive Connected Nations report, and republished on ONS's 'Explore local statistics' service as the 'Gigabit-capable broadband' indicator, Jan 2026 vintage), but neither page exposes a plain-text local figure. thinkbroadband's local broadband statistics for Lewisham - built from Ofcom's own postcode-level open coverage data - gives 80.96% full-fibre coverage as of 17 July 2026, and is used as the Lewisham-specific figure instead of the UK-wide one previously shown here. No ward-level breakdown exists; borough is the most granular level available.

indicator: 5G mobile coverage (% of landmass, at least one operator)
notes: Original indicator label ('Mobile coverage data') renamed to match what's actually reported. A Lewisham-specific figure is now confirmed and used instead of the England-wide one previously shown here: 99.8% of Lewisham's geographic area has outdoor 5G signal from at least one operator, per Ofcom Connected Nations data (January 2026), published via ONS's 'Explore local statistics' local-authority indicator - same metric definition as the England figure it replaces. The live ONS/Ofcom pages are still blocked under this session's network policy, so the figure is sourced from search-engine snippets of those pages plus independent corroboration from a third-party aggregator (connection-technologies.co.uk), hence 'medium' rather than 'high' confidence. No ward-level breakdown exists; borough is the most granular figure available.

Original indicator label ('Digital exclusion data') renamed to match what's actually reported, then renamed again when the underlying metric changed. The GLA/LOTI 'Mapping Digital Exclusion' dataset previously cited here is genuinely limited to five pilot boroughs (Barnet, Brent, Kensington & Chelsea, Southwark, Westminster) - Lewisham isn't covered and no Lewisham-specific output exists from it. Switched to GMCA's Digital Exclusion Risk Index (DERI) v1.5, which scores every LSOA in Great Britain: Ladywell's figure (2.5/10) is the population-weighted average of its 7 constituent LSOAs' individual DERI scores (Great-Britain-normalised, England IMD basis - the only DERI variant comparable across areas). The GLA's 2022 London-wide estimate (c.270,000 Londoners completely offline) is kept as descriptive context in the pipeline source notes rather than as the snapshot, since it measures a different thing (headcount vs. relative risk).

Underlying source: ONS Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) via NOMIS. Re-verified 2026-07-17: Lewisham's 80:20 hourly wage ratio is 2.43 vs England's 1.52 average. Trust for London's page shows a 'last updated January 2026' stamp reporting pay inequality has fallen in most London boroughs since the prior release (Lewisham not named among the four exceptions), but this session's WebFetch/curl tools were blocked by the environment's egress policy for trustforlondon.org.uk and ons.gov.uk, so neither the exact updated value nor the multi-year trend behind the interactive chart could be extracted - a follow-up session with working page-fetch access should re-check both.

No Lewisham- or borough-level wealth distribution figure exists (ONS's Wealth and Assets Survey - WAS - isn't designed to support reliable local authority estimates). Uses the GLA's London-wide figure instead: bottom half of London households hold 4% of the capital's total wealth. Underlying source: ONS Wealth and Assets Survey microdata via the GLA's Economic Fairness programme. Caveat: the Office for Statistics Regulation removed WAS's Official Statistics accreditation in June 2025, citing insufficient quality - treat as indicative. An older, now-archived Trust for London page (trustforlondon.org.uk/data/wealth-distribution/, 2018-2020 WAS data) put London's bottom-half wealth share at 6.8% and England's poorest-50%-share at 9%; not used as the headline figure here since it's no longer updated, but kept as background context.

Split out from the former combined 'Pay gap (ethnic, gender)' row - gender and ethnicity pay gaps come from different ONS surveys (ASHE vs Annual Population Survey) and are genuinely distinct measures, so combining them into one number would have hidden more than it showed. No Lewisham-specific figure found (ONS ASHE Table 8 could in principle produce a residence-based local authority figure, but this session's tools could not reach ons.gov.uk to extract it). Uses the GLA's London-wide figure: women's mean hourly pay was 14% below men's in 2023. Underlying source: ONS Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE).
